headline: One dead, one critical and one missing after Manchester-by-the-Sea boat crash
dek: A 67-year-old man died after a fishing boat went into distress off Singing Beach; a 65-year-old was hospitalized and a 37-year-old remained missing in the latest public updates.
body: A boating incident off Manchester-by-the-Sea left one man dead, another in critical condition and a third missing in the latest public updates Sunday. The three men had been aboard a 30-foot center-console fishing boat with a dog before the vessel went into distress near Singing Beach, according to officials cited by [NBC Boston](https://www.nbcboston.com/news/local/manchester-by-the-sea-ma-boat-incident-singing-beach-search/4025412/). The dog was found alive.

The U.S. Coast Guard received a distress report shortly before 4:30 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 3. [Boston 25 News](https://cmg-cmg-tv-10020-prod.cdn.arcpublishing.com/news/local/one-person-dead-another-missing-after-vessel-distress-near-manchester-by-sea/UGXXSUHHSRBZBGPCAO63MRI6AE/) reported that the call described a boat spinning out of control and striking rocks. [WCVB](https://www.wcvb.com/article/boat-crashes-coast-manchester-by-the-sea-three-people-pulled-water/74008842) also reported the Coast Guard account that the boat hit rocks before responders reached the scene at about 4:48 p.m.

Rescuers located two men in the water. NBC Boston reported that the 67-year-old was taken to Beverly Hospital, where he was pronounced dead, while the 65-year-old was flown by medical helicopter to Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston. Officials had not publicly released the men’s names in the reports reviewed for this article. Their conditions and identities remain separate questions from the investigation into how the incident unfolded.

The third man, identified by officials only as 37 years old, remained missing after the initial search. Multiple agencies joined the response, including Coast Guard units from Station Gloucester and Air Station Cape Cod, the Massachusetts State Police, local harbor masters, the Boston Harbormaster, the Beverly Fire Department dive team, Gloucester police and the Massachusetts Environmental Police. [WHDH 7News](https://whdh.com/news/coast-guard-assisting-with-search-for-missing-boater-off-manchester-by-the-sea/) reported Saturday night that more than a dozen boats and a Coast Guard helicopter were involved in the effort.

The response stretched across the North Shore because the scene sits in active coastal waters off Cape Ann, where local police, harbor departments and federal search-and-rescue crews can operate together. That regional coordination is important in a case where a person may be difficult to locate from shore and where weather, currents and the condition of the vessel can change the search area. The agencies’ presence confirms the scale of the operation; it does not establish why the boat lost control or whether a mechanical problem, a collision or another factor was involved.

Officials were still investigating the circumstances. NBC Boston reported that the initial 911 call said the boat was taking on water, while the vessel was not sunk when crews arrived. Boston 25 reported that officials described the boat as having crashed into rocks. Those accounts establish the emergency response and reported impact, but they do not amount to a final determination of cause. No source reviewed for this report announced an arrest, a citation or a completed marine investigation.

The latest confirmed picture is therefore limited: one man died, one was critically injured, one remained unaccounted for and the dog survived. The public reports did not identify the boat’s owner, explain the men’s relationships or say when the search would end. Families and investigators will need more information before the incident can be described beyond the known rescue, medical and search operations. Residents and boaters should rely on updates from the Coast Guard, local authorities and the district attorney’s office rather than unverified reports while the search and investigation continue.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Manchester-by-the-Sea boat crash leaves one dead and one missing
